title: {Syn} Wilson Theorem Turns Factorials Into Primality Clues
content:
Wilson theorem says that n is prime exactly when (n - 1)! is congruent to -1 modulo n. It is a beautiful characterization of primality.

As a test it is usually impractical, because factorials get huge quickly. As a theorem it neatly captures how residues pair with their inverses modulo a prime.

Why it matters: number theory keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
